life_summary: Gordon Bitner Hinckley was born June 23, 1910, in Salt Lake City, Utah, to a prominent church and business family. His father, Bryant S. Hinckley, was a successful businessman and church leader, providing Gordon with a cultured, educated family environment. Hinckley attended the University of Utah and later studied at Oxford University as a visiting student, bringing international educational experience to his formation. Before his full-time ecclesiastical service, he worked in business and public relations, including employment with the church's public communications office. He developed exceptional skills in public speaking, writing, and media relations that would distinguish his later ecclesiastical career. Hinckley earned respect as an articulate, forward-thinking communicator across secular and religious spheres.
church_summary: Hinckley served as an LDS missionary in the British Mission (1933–1935) from London. Ordained an apostle in 1961, he advanced through leadership positions including counselor to church presidents. He became church president in 1995 and led until his death in 2008, serving nearly thirteen years. During his presidency, Hinckley dedicated or rededicated 92 temples overall, with 65 additional dedications and five rededications as president, dramatically expanding the church's temple network. He authored 'The Family: A Proclamation to the World' (1995), a foundational statement on family values. Hinckley championed the Perpetual Education Fund (2001) to assist members in developing nations, education accessibility, humanitarian aid, and six personal virtues: gratitude, intelligence, cleanliness, honesty, humility, and prayerfulness.
